script.title: Why KFC Operator Made Only ₹3.4 Cr Profit #shorts

segments.text: Ever wondered why your ₹500 KFC bucket barely leaves any profit for the company?
segments.broll: fast food counter fried chicken close up
broll_alt: person holding crispy fried chicken slice

segments.text: KFC and Pizza Hut operator Devyani International saw quarterly revenue jump 10%, yet net profit crashed to just ₹3.4 crore.
segments.broll: hand holding indian rupee notes close up

segments.text: So where is all your fast-food paisa actually going?
broll_alt: cooking oil pouring in pan close up

segments.text: First, rising costs for chicken, cheese, and cooking oil ate up a huge chunk of total sales.
segments.broll: raw chicken pieces kitchen prep wide

segments.text: Second, heavy shopping mall rents and aggressive new store expansion strained their balance sheet.
broll_alt: store front glass window retail street

segments.text: Plus, deep discounts to lure budget diners squeezed profit margins even further.
broll_alt: person looking at digital menu board
crowded fast food restaurant dining room

segments.text: Educational framing only, not financial advice, but running food giants in India is a tough game.
segments.broll: busy city street traffic night timelapse

script.description: Ever wondered where your fast-food money goes? Devyani International, the operator behind KFC and Pizza Hut in India, reported a net profit of just ₹3.4 crore despite revenue growing over 10%. Here is the economics breakdown behind quick service restaurants in India. #KFCIndia #DevyaniInternational #IndianBusiness

facts_to_verify.claim: Devyani International Q2 net profit stood at ₹3.4 crore with revenue up 10.6%

script.chosen_candidate: Devyani International Q2 results: Net profit at ₹3.4 cr, revenue up 10.6% - Business Standard
script.why_it_will_work: Household fast-food brands like KFC and Pizza Hut create immediate familiarity, while a tiny ₹3.4 crore profit on huge revenue triggers deep curiosity about business economics.
